speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast syndrome.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, significant unexplained weight loss, and your history of smoking strongly suggests a lung apex tumor compressing the brachial plexus and sympathetic chain. Given your age and smoking history, I suspect lung cancer; please undergo a CT scan of the chest immediately to confirm.
